title: Automorphism pullback preserves constructible categories at every coefficient stage
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in it, with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and let $e:T\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ be an automorphism of schemes, not necessarily a $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. At finite coefficients use constant sheaves $(A_n)_T$ on the small pro-etale site; integrally use $\widehat R_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ and the canonical coefficient isomorphism $c_e:e^{-1}\widehat R_T\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat R_T$ induced by the constant quotient maps [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Use the categories $D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$ for $\Lambda=A_n,R,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

At each of these four stages, the prescribed pullback $F_e=Le^*$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] restricts to a coefficient-linear exact equivalence of $D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$, inverse to $F_{e^{-1}}$, with the canonical inverse-composition and shift comparisons. At finite coefficients it sends a witnessing partition $(S_\nu)$ for a cohomology sheaf to $(e^{-1}S_\nu)$ and preserves the same cohomological interval. Integrally ordinary module pullback along $c_e$ agrees with completed pullback through its actual completion comparison, preserves derived completeness, and satisfies
$$(F_eK)\otimes^L_{\widehat R_T}(A_n)_T\cong F_{e,n}(K\otimes^L_{\widehat R_T}(A_n)_T).$$
These natural isomorphisms commute with all quotient transitions, completion units and finite projection maps; hence the same uniform interval for the reductions is preserved. The rational and algebraically closed equivalences are respectively its rationalization and coherent finite-field descent.

If $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ are complementary immersions of separated finite-type $k$-schemes and automorphisms $e_X,e_Z,e_U$ satisfy $e_Xi=ie_Z$ and $e_Xj=je_U$, pullback composition gives natural isomorphisms
$$b:F_{e_U}j^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*F_{e_X},\qquad d:F_{e_Z}i^*\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*F_{e_X}.$$
They are coherent with identities, inverse automorphisms, shifts, finite reduction, rationalization and common-stage scalar extension. In particular these assertions apply to the geometric-Frobenius automorphisms of [def-weil-frobenius-detailed].

proof.text: Put $G_e=e^{-1}$ with the canonical constant coefficient action. By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], on an object $V\to T$ this is reindexing $M(V\to T)\mapsto M(V\xrightarrow e T)$, with inverse reindexing by $e^{-1}$. Both send covering families to covering families. The constant-section comparison fixes every $a\in A_n$, so reindexing is $A_n$-linear on morphisms. This exact equivalence on module sheaves induces an exact functor on the unbounded derived categories by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. The finite pullback prescribed in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is precisely this termwise functor; its inverse is the one for $e^{-1}$.

proof.text:
Let $M$ be a cohomology sheaf and $(S_
u)$ a witnessing partition in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Restrict the isomorphism $e$ to $e^{-1}S_
u\xrightarrow\sim S_
u$. Inverse images of the finitely many locally closed constructible pieces are again such pieces, disjoint and covering $T$. Reindexing a covering which trivializes $M|_{S_
u}$ trivializes its inverse image with the identical finite $A_n$-module. Thus this is the required partition. By [lem-pur-proetale-constant-module-pullback-homology], $\mathcal H^a(F_{e,n}K)\cong e_n^*\mathcal H^a(K)$. If the latter sheaf is zero outside $[r,s]$, so is the former; apply the same argument to $e^{-1}$ for the inverse. This proves the finite restriction to $D^b_c$ with the same interval.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] for finite compositors, with the coefficient equations of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. The identity is precisely the termwise comparison of [lem-pur-proetale-derived-pullback-identity]. The module compositor is the comparison of left adjoints to the base-change direct-image identification by [lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition]. For three maps, the two direct-image comparisons identify either parenthesized iterated fibre product with the same fibre product, carrying its projections identically. They therefore agree by the fibre-product universal property. Now [lem-trf-adjoint-composition-coherence] gives associativity of these specified left-adjoint comparisons. The identity equations follow by the same unit normalization with an identity fibre product. The localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] carries these termwise equations to derived functors. Shifts reindex the same component maps. Substituting $(e,e^{-1})$ gives the inverse-composition comparisons. For $e_Xj=je_U$, compose the compositor for $j\circ e_U$ with the inverse compositor for $e_X\circ j$ to obtain $b$; use $i$ for $d$. Their identity, inverse and shift equations are instances of these composition equations.

source.place: Weil-structures paragraph, first two sentences; agent expansion using the cited general lemmas

proof.text: Integrally write $B=\widehat R_T$ and let $H_e$ be ordinary module pullback along $c_e$. The reindexing in [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] transports the $B$-module action through $c_e$ and has inverse using $c_{e^{-1}}$: their composites act as the identity on both sections and scalars, by the composition equation in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. It is therefore an exact equivalence also for these nonconstant coefficient sheaves, preserving products, kernels and cokernels by reindexing. It induces an exact derived equivalence by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. The strict-tower comparison of [lem-pur-integral-ambient-operation-models] identifies $(H_eK)_n$ with $F_{e,n}K_n$ and identifies quotient augmentations and transitions. Apply $H_e$ to a completeness Roos triangle from [def-weil-derived-complete]: products become products, $1-s$ becomes the $1-s$ of this identified reduction tower, and its first map remains the family of quotient maps. Thus $H_eK$ is derived complete whenever $K$ is; the same holds for its inverse.

source.place: Weil-structures paragraph, first two sentences; agent expansion using the cited general lemmas

proof.text: For complete $K$ the SPECIFIED ordinary-to-completed comparison is invertible by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization]: its factorization is $\theta_{e,K}\kappa^e_K=H_e(u_K)$. Hence the prescribed completed $F_e$ agrees with $H_e$ through this actual comparison. By [lem-pur-integral-ambient-operation-models], on a flat-term K-flat representative the reduction comparison is the balanced tensor map on the entire quotient tower, not a choice of maps between its cohomology objects. Its augmentation is the specified map, with zero shifted-product coordinate. Consequently the resulting isomorphisms $(F_eK)\otimes_B^L(A_n)_T\cong F_{e,n}(K_n)$ commute with quotient transitions, the finite projections and completion units. Together with Step 2 and completeness from Step 4, the definition [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] gives $F_eK\in D^b_c(T,R)$, preserving the SAME uniform $[r,s]$.

proof.text: The integral restrictions are exact inverse equivalences by Steps 4–5. They are $R$-linear: the equation $\pi_nc_e=c_{e,n}e^{-1}\pi_n$ fixes every constant scalar $r$ at each quotient, hence its image in $B$; on sections $H_e(rf)=rH_e(f)$. For $b,d$ use the two integral compositors of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] for $j\circ e_U=e_X\circ j$ or $i\circ e_Z=e_X\circ i$; this supplies associativity and their finite reduction formulas. To check the full-map equations, use [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution], which explicitly identifies the canonical completed compositor with the limit of the adjunction-normalized WHOLE-SYSTEM compositor, compatibly with substitution. Its normalization hypothesis holds for the reduction system of any input $K$: take the single flat-term K-flat representative used above. Its scalar extensions $Q_m$ stay K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] applied to the identity topos and the quotient coefficient map. Thus $Q_m\otimes_{A_m}A_n=Q_n$ computes the transition adjoint; multiplication of scalar factors gives its identity and cocycle equations. Step 5 identifies $K$ with its actual reconstruction. Step 3's equations then hold on the finite system maps: the two sides have identical scalar-association components and transitions on these representatives. Apply the total-limit functor and the substitution comparisons of the tower-substitution lemma. This gives identity, inverse and shift equations for the actual integral maps and their completion and reduction comparisons, without assuming that finite reductions are jointly faithful on morphisms.

proof.text:
For $E\subset L$ write $T_W$ for the COMPLETED integral scalar extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For $f=e,e^{-1},i,j$ use the framework comparison $\theta_f:T_XF_{f,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f,L}T_Y$ of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], normalized by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. All schemes have $\ell$ invertible since they are $k$-schemes and $\ell\ne p$; every input is constructible and derived complete by Steps 4–6. No etale-origin witness and no $k$-linearity of $e$ is required. The realization lemma gives, for $h:Z\to W$, $k:W\to V$,
$$F_{h,L}(\theta_k)\circ\theta_h F_{k,E}\circ T_Z(c^E_{h,k})=c^L_{h,k}T_V\circ\theta_{kh}.$$
Apply this twice to the equal maps $j e_U=e_Xj$; cancelling the invertible compositors gives the scalar square for $b$ defined in Step 6. With $i$ it gives the square for $d$, and with $(e,e^{-1})$ it gives the inverse-composition square. The same lemma gives units and the successive-field associator equations for these actual comparisons. The shift equation for these specified $\theta_f$, which is not asserted by that realization lemma, is [lem-sf-framework-theta-shift-compatibility]. Thus these are coherent comparisons for the framework completed operations.

source.place: Weil-structures paragraph, first two sentences; agent expansion using the cited general lemmas

proof.text: By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], rationalization has the integral objects, morphisms $\operatorname{Hom}(K,M)\otimes_R E$, the induced shift, and distinguished triangles isomorphic to images of integral distinguished triangles. An $R$-linear exact functor $F$ from Steps 4–6 therefore extends by $F(u\otimes a)=F(u)\otimes a$: the balancing relation follows from $R$-linearity; composition and identities follow on pure tensors and then by additivity. Its linearized shift comparison carries every image integral triangle to a distinguished triangle, and hence every distinguished triangle to one. Integral natural transformations extend by their same components; naturality and their composition, inverse and shift equations extend by bilinearity. The integral immersion pullbacks $i^*,j^*$ of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] are also $R$-linear and exact: on flat-term K-flat representatives they are the functorial $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ of termwise additive functors (reduction, $f^*$, $\operatorname{Res}_n$, products), which carry the termwise split sequence $0\to Q\to C(u)\to P[1]\to0$ of a cone to a termwise split sequence, hence a cone triangle to a distinguished triangle, with the shift comparison obtained by shifting the representative and its tower. Apply this to $F_e,F_{e^{-1}},i^*,j^*$, their inverse comparisons, $b,d$, and Step 7's $\theta$ squares. These are precisely the rational operations on objects and pure tensors in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Consequently the equivalence and all equations hold in the FRAMEWORK $D^b_c(T,E)$; no identification with a different rational category is used.

source.place: Weil-structures paragraph, first two sentences; agent expansion using the cited general lemmas

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-framework-common-stage-descent] to the exact rational functors from Step 8 with $\beta=\theta$ rationalized. Step 7 gives its unit and associator equations and the theta shift lemma gives its shift hypothesis; the framework scalar transitions are exact by [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated]. For a representative $u$ over $L$, descent sends it to $\theta_{E',L}^{-1}F_{e,L}(u)\theta_{E,L}$. Both this formula and the object $(E,F_{e,E}K)$ are exactly those prescribed at algebraically closed coefficients in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], using [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Thus the descended equivalence is the specified $F_e$. Descend $F_{e^{-1}}$ and the compatible inverse transformations to obtain its inverse. The same comparison of formulas, with $\theta_i,\theta_j$ (Steps 7–8 and the theta shift lemma for $f=i,j$), shows that the exact families $i^*_E,j^*_E$ descend to the prescribed $i^*,j^*$. For $b$, apply descent to the composite families $F_{e_U}j^*$ and $j^*F_{e_X}$, with the whiskered composite comparisons; the composition clause of the descent lemma identifies their descended functors with these composites of prescribed functors. Step 7 is exactly the scalar-compatibility square for $b_E$ (in the $(h,k)$ notation of Step 7, $b_E=c^E_{j,e_X}\circ(c^E_{e_U,j})^{-1}$), so its class gives the prescribed pullback-composition $b$; the same applies to $d$. Descent preserves their shift, identity, inverse and associativity equations from Steps 3 and 6. It gives exactness and independence of the common field. Its $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-linearity follows over one finite field containing the finitely many scalars and representative arrows, where every functor is linear.

proof.text: Finally [def-weil-frobenius-detailed] supplies the geometric-Frobenius scheme automorphisms on geometric fibres from finite-field models. For complementary immersions from the same model the two squares commute already by the base-change definition $g=\mathrm{id}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$. They therefore satisfy exactly the scheme-automorphism hypotheses used above, even though they need not be $k$-morphisms. Substituting these automorphisms gives the final specialization.

proof.text: Lean implementation of the equivalence and constructibility clauses: characteristic p and the structure maps make ell a unit. The termwise isomorphism-pullback interface gives finite constructibility and interval preservation; restrict it to the full constructible subcategory and use the fully faithful shift lift. Transport fixed-scalar linearity through the intrinsic realization. Pull back each witnessing stratum and its finite local trivialization. Specialize the existing isomorphism-field transport interface to e and its inverse for integral, rational and common-stage exact equivalences. The raw rational tensor functor is identified with scalar localization of the integral functor to prove localization-ring linearity. Use the normalized ordinary/completed comparison, the legacy-completeness equivalence and the finite reduction models for completeness and the unchanged uniform interval. Specialize the existing whole-system pullback comparison to obtain the prescribed reductions. Remaining coherence and raw shift obligations retain the preceding proof plan.

proof.text: A4 stage-3 implementation: construct the normalized integral compositor as a natural isomorphism using the pullback realization, the effective whole-system counit and the sequence compositor. Restrict to the full constructible subcategories. Compose its inverse with equality transport and the other compositor to obtain the integral square; component extensionality proves uniqueness. Extend this natural isomorphism through raw scalar localization, proving naturality on pure tensors and then by additive induction; its component formula proves uniqueness. Apply the two scalar/composition equations and cancel the invertible compositors to prove the integral scalar square. Finally apply the prescribed common-stage map formula to a scalar multiple of a represented arrow, and use finite-stage functor linearity and bilinearity of composition. For finite coherence identify the specified square with the derived module square, derive its identity and horizontal pasting equations, and cancel the derived compositors to obtain the inverse equation. The derived compositor and equality transport respect shifts. These close the integral square, rational square, finite coherence, scalar square, and common-stage linearity clauses; all other unfinished clauses retain the earlier proof plan.

B5 stage-3 implementation of the entire-system reduction square: write R for the target reduction, L for its right adjoint total limit, epsilon for their counit, a_g for the prescribed pullback realization and delta_g = R(a_g) followed by epsilon for the prescribed effective system comparison. Counit naturality gives R(eta_{h,k}) followed by epsilon = delta_h followed by U_h(delta_k). The defining equation c_{h,k} followed by eta_{h,k} = a_{hk} followed by L(s_{h,k}), together with counit naturality for s_{h,k}, therefore gives R(c_{h,k}) followed by delta_h and U_h(delta_k) = delta_{hk} followed by s_{h,k}. Apply this equation to (e_Y,f) and (f,e_X). Substitute the specified integral square c_{e_Y,f}^{-1} followed by equality transport and c_{f,e_X}; transport of delta along the given equality of scheme maps follows by equality induction. Cancel R(c_{e_Y,f}) and the system compositor to obtain the required equality with the specified system square. This uses the whole quotient diagram and its actual counit; it does not assume faithfulness of the separate finite reductions. Other unfinished clauses retain the preceding plan.
